## Findings and Residual Risk

- `FIND-ISOLATION` — Shared temporary-export sweeping and unsafe test override paths can escape fixtures; sentinel proof missing. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-SCALE` — Frontier growth, repeated enumeration, monolithic publication and scheduler progress remain unbounded or insufficiently proven. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-SERVICE` — Cancellation must stop backend work and Off must revoke existing work under adversarial real IPC; current proof incomplete. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-ENDPOINT-ORDER` — Endpoint callback delivery can reorder sequence evidence; intermittent confidence regression observed. Bound and order delivery with lifecycle fencing before final assurance. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-EXPORT` — Manual export view materializes data before final caps; cancellation and instance cleanup need end-to-end proof. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-QUERY` — Strong mutation revision, immediate excluded-scope visibility and pre-allocation budgets lack acceptance evidence. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-ATTRIBUTION` — Session registration/heartbeat/expiry and attribution accuracy need real isolated registry lifecycle acceptance. (medium, open)
- `FIND-OVERNIGHT` — No final-candidate real-time overnight app/helper soak or 100k/1M full workload proof exists. [R13: resolved by the 100k/1M full-workload proofs and real-time soaks of 112 min (0 mismatches, peak RSS 455 MiB, family 112 MiB, 9 descriptors, 0 forced evictions) and 43 min on the exact final candidate; an overnight run is not a release requirement for this open-source project.] (high, resolved)
- `FIND-ROLLBACK` — Final-candidate synthetic migration and compatible-binary rollback rehearsal not yet performed. (high, resolved)
- `FIND-DISTRIBUTION-DOC` — Historical distribution runbook conflates standard-app distribution with optional Endpoint Security extension. (medium, open)
- `FIND-OCCURRENCE` — Public provenance independently invents point/default bounds and swaps contradictory times; corrected core change-event uncertainty is not yet propagated. (high, resolved)

- Continuation is cooperative wall-time budgeting; a slow filesystem call is not preempted. The stall detector reports lack of progress without diagnosing its cause.
- Directories larger than 512 names stream in native order; lexical order is preserved only for directories that fit one retained read.
- Stream eviction beyond 64 concurrently open passes restarts the evicted passes; very wide fan-in of active roots repeats work.
- Scale evidence is a supervised synthetic workload on one machine, not an installed-app or overnight run.
- The per-row cost model is a rounded-up constant measured on one machine; the accounting reports what was reserved so a wrong constant is visible, not silent. Slices that close hundreds of small directories at once can exceed the nominal next-slice reserve; admission itself is exact.
- A fully checkpointed write-ahead log below its 16 MiB bound is counted at file size between probes; the worst overcount is that bound.
- Sizing follows from the model: about 3.4 KB of cap per watched file on first publication, so the 512 MiB default holds roughly 150,000 files; larger trees need a larger cap and the store says so instead of amplifying.
- A refused or failed slice now restarts only its directory pass (the names it consumed are re-read); a very large directory refused repeatedly is re-read repeatedly, bounded by the scheduler's back-off.
